Species</strong></h2><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">This biodiverse region is home to several rare and spectacular bird species that make <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Costa Rica birding</strong> truly world-class. These are the species that bring photographers and birders from around the globe:</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Turquoise Cotinga - The Crown Jewel</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">The <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Turquoise Cotinga</strong> is one of the most spectacular and range-restricted birds in Central America. Listed as Vulnerable by IUCN with only 1,250-2,820 mature individuals worldwide, this electric-blue cotinga is found nowhere else on Earth except Costa Rica&#x27;s Pacific slope and western Panama. </p><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7"><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">The Osa Peninsula represents this species&#x27; primary stronghold</strong>, and sightings around lodges with fruiting trees are regular during the right season. Males are an almost iridescent turquoise-blue with purple patches: truly unforgettable when spotted against the green canopy.</p><figure class="relative mt-0"><img alt="turquise cotinga seen near the font-bold">King Vulture - The Magnificent Scavenger</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">While other regions of Costa Rica have largely lost this spectacular species, the <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">King Vulture</strong> remains reliably present on the Osa Peninsula. With its enormous wingspan (up to 2 meters), pristine white plumage, and psychedelic multi-colored head featuring orange, yellow, red, and purple, this is arguably the most beautiful vulture in the world. Often seen soaring high above the forest canopy or perched in emergent trees, spotting a King Vulture is a highlight of any Osa birding trip.</p><figure class="relative mt-0"><img alt="king vulture text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 flex items-center"><span class="block mt-0.5 lg:ml-auto"><span>© <!-- -->Katia Hollaar</span></span></figcaption></figure><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Baird&#x27;s Trogon - The Regional Endemic</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">A stunning regional endemic found only on Costa Rica&#x27;s southern Pacific slope and western Panama, <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Baird&#x27;s Trogon</strong> is one of the top target species for birders visiting Osa. Males feature brilliant plumage with a distinctive blue eye ring and barred undertail pattern. Patient observers in foothill and mid-elevation forests are often rewarded with excellent views.</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Collared Forest-Falcon - The Jungle Ghost</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">The <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Collared Forest-Falcon</strong> embodies the mystery of the rainforest. This large, powerful raptor with striking black and white barring and distinctive &quot;collar&quot; is heard far more often than seen. Its haunting, hollow <em>&quot;ow&quot;</em> call echoes through the jungle at dawn. When spotted, it reveals itself as a masterful ambush hunter, pursuing prey on foot through the understory with remarkable agility. Getting clear photographs of this cryptic species is considered a major achievement.</p><figure class="relative mt-0"><img alt="collared forest-falcon" loading="lazy" width="1353" height="2029" font-bold">Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager - The Ultra-Endemic</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">The <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager</strong> is a very rare bird endemic exclusively to the Osa Peninsula and Golfo Dulce region. class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">The Icons: Macaws and Toucans</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">And of course, not to miss the loud, spectacular <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Scarlet Macaws</strong> flying above the canopy in pairs, one of the most sought-after subjects for <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">wildlife photography</strong>. The large and vocal <strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Chestnut-mandibled Toucan</strong> (also called Yellow-throated Toucan) perched on nearby branches provides equally impressive photo opportunities. These charismatic species are seen daily around most Osa lodges.</p><figure class="relative mt-0"><img alt="scarlet macaw in flight" loading="lazy" width="3927" height="2619" decoding="async" font-bold">Frequently Asked Questions About Osa Peninsula Birdwatching</strong></h2><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">How many bird species can I see in Osa Peninsula?</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">Over 400 bird species have been recorded in the Osa Peninsula region, including resident species, migrants, and rare endemics. Serious birders can expect to see 100-150 species during a week-long visit.</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">What are the most iconic birds to photograph in Osa Peninsula?</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">Scarlet Macaws, Chestnut-mandibled Toucans, and the endemic Mangrove Hummingbird top most photographers&#x27; lists. The rare Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager and Turquoise Cotinga are also highly sought-after.</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Is Osa Peninsula good for beginner birdwatchers?</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">Absolutely! Large, colorful species like Scarlet Macaws, toucans, and tanagers are easy to spot and identify, making it perfect for beginners while still offering challenges for experts.</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">When is the best time for bird photography in Costa Rica&#x27;s Osa Peninsula?</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">The dry season (December-April) offers the best lighting conditions and trail access, though the wet season (May-November) provides dramatic skies and fewer tourists.</p><h3><strong class="dark:text-zinc-100 font-bold">Plan Your Osa Peninsula Birding Adventure</strong></h3><p class="portable-text-p mb-6 leading-7">So, prepare your cameras and pack your binoculars: Osa Peninsula, Costa Rica awaits!</p><figure class="relative mt-0"><img alt="a couple of scarlet macaws flying over the jungle" loading="lazy" width="3261" height="2174" decoding="async" data-nimg="1"
